svg.aria-label: A signal handler calling printf deadlocks on the allocator lock held by the interrupted code
svg.text: Why printf in a signal handler can deadlock
the handler interrupts code that holds a lock it then needs
main code: malloc() → takes the allocator lock → updating free lists…
SIGALRM handler: printf("tick") → malloc() → wait for allocator lock
the lock is held by the same thread, which can't continue until the handler returns → deadlock
Or worse: no lock, and the handler sees half-updated data structures and corrupts them. That's why POSIX defines
a short list of async-signal-safe functions (write, _exit, kill, sigaction, read and a few dozen more).
printf, malloc, free, most of stdio, locks, and anything that might use them are not on it.
